note.answer: A thermometer measures temperature using a thermometric property that changes with temperature.

options: It is a property that remains unchanged when temperature changes.
It is a property that changes appreciably when temperature changes.
It is the amount of heat stored in a body.

This is correct because thermometers use a property that changes appreciably with temperature.

rationales: This is correct because the steam point is the upper fixed point.
This is incorrect because the ice point is the lower fixed point.

rationales: This is incorrect because 100 equal parts are used on the Celsius and Kelvin scales.

This is incorrect because 273 is the Kelvin value assigned to the ice point in the textbook.

This is incorrect because this formula converts Celsius to Kelvin.
This is incorrect because the Fahrenheit-to-Celsius formula uses T_f − 32, not T_c − 32.

written.text: What is meant by thermometric property of a substance? Enlist some thermometric properties.
written.finalAnswer: A thermometric property is a property of a substance that changes appreciably with temperature. Examples include the volume of a liquid, the pressure of a gas, the resistance of a wire and the thermo-electric current in a thermocouple.

rubric.why: The definition must identify a property that changes with temperature.
rubric.how: Explain that the property changes appreciably with temperature.

rubric.why: Relevant examples show how the property can be used to measure temperature.
rubric.how: Name at least one valid example such as liquid volume, gas pressure or wire resistance.

modelAnswer: A thermometric property is a property of a substance that changes appreciably with temperature.
Examples are the volume of a liquid, the pressure of a gas, the resistance of a wire and the thermo-electric current in a thermocouple.

written.text: Why is mercury usually preferred to alcohol as a thermometric liquid?
written.finalAnswer: Mercury does not wet glass, is opaque and easily visible because of its silvery colour, and has uniform expansion. Alcohol must be coloured to make it visible.

written.finalAnswer: Water is not suitable because it has non-linear expansion. 373 K is equivalent to 100°C and 212°F.

written.text: What is temperature? How is it measured? Describe briefly the construction of a mercury-in-glass thermometer.
written.finalAnswer: Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of a body. It is measured with a thermometer using a thermometric property. A mercury-in-glass thermometer is made of glass and has a bulb at one end filled with mercury, joined to a narrow capillary tube and a scale. As temperature rises, mercury expands and moves up the capillary; the position of the end of the thread gives the temperature.

rubric.why: The answer must state what temperature represents.
rubric.how: Describe it as the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.

rubric.why: The measuring instrument and its basis should be identified.
rubric.how: State that a thermometer uses a thermometric property.

rubric.why: The bulb and mercury are essential parts of the instrument.

rubric.why: The narrow tube allows the expanded liquid to rise visibly.
rubric.how: Mention the narrow capillary tube and scale.

rubric.why: The operating principle connects mercury's rise to the temperature reading.
rubric.how: State that heated mercury rises in the capillary and its end position reads the temperature.

modelAnswer: Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
For the exact measurement of the hotness of a substance, we require an instrument called a thermometer.
A mercury-in-glass thermometer is made of glass and has a bulb at one end filled with mercury.
The bulb is connected to a narrow capillary tube, and a scale is marked on the glass stem.
When the temperature rises, the mercury expands and moves up through the capillary tube; the position of the end of the thread reads the temperature.

written.text: Compare the three scales used for measuring temperature.
written.finalAnswer: Celsius: ice point 0°C, steam point 100°C, 100 divisions. Fahrenheit: ice point 32°F, steam point 212°F, 180 divisions. Kelvin: ice point 273 K, steam point 373 K, 100 divisions; it is also called the absolute temperature scale.

modelAnswer: In Celsius scale, the lower and upper fixed points are 0°C and 100°C; the space between them is divided into 100 equal parts.
In Fahrenheit scale, the lower and upper fixed points are 32°F and 212°F; the space between them is divided into 180 equal parts.
In Kelvin scale, the lower and upper fixed points are 273 K and 373 K; the space between them is divided into 100 equal parts.
The width of 1 K is the same as that of 1°C.
Kelvin is also known as the absolute temperature scale and is used in scientific measurements.

explain.title: Why a thermometer is needed
explain.body: Our sense of touch can tell us whether something feels hot or cold, but it cannot measure the exact temperature. A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature. Thermometers use some property of a substance, which changes appreciably with the change of temperature.

explain.title: Choosing a thermometric material
explain.body: Some basic thermometric properties for a material suitable to construct a thermometer are the following: It is a good conductor of heat; it gives quick response to temperature changes; it has uniform thermal expansion; it has high boiling point; it has low freezing point; it has large expansivity (low specific heat capacity); it does not wet glass; it does not vapourize; it is visible.

explain.title: Liquid-in-glass thermometers
explain.body: Liquids expand on heating, so the expansion in the volume of a liquid can be used to measure temperature. A liquid-in-glass thermometer has a glass bulb filled with liquid and a narrow capillary tube. As the temperature rises, the liquid expands and moves up the tube. The position of the end of the liquid thread gives the temperature. Mercury is opaque and easy to see; alcohol must be coloured to make it visible.

explain.title: Fixed points and temperature scales
explain.body: A temperature scale is constructed using two reference temperatures called fixed points. The steam point is the upper fixed point and the melting point of pure ice is the lower fixed point. Celsius assigns 0 and 100 to these points; Fahrenheit assigns 32 and 212; Kelvin assigns 273 and 373. Kelvin is also called the absolute temperature scale.

explain.title: Converting temperatures
explain.body: For Celsius to Fahrenheit use T_f = 9/5 × T_c + 32. For Fahrenheit to Celsius use T_c = 5/9 (T_f − 32). For Celsius to Kelvin use T_k = T_c + 273. Substitute the given value into the appropriate formula and include the correct unit in your answer.

explain.title: Thermocouple thermometers
explain.body: A thermocouple has two wires made of different materials joined to form two junctions. When the junctions are at different temperatures, a small current and potential difference are produced. A greater temperature difference produces a greater potential difference. Thermocouples are useful for very high temperatures and rapidly changing temperatures.

mistakes: Do not confuse the lower fixed point with the upper fixed point: the ice point is lower and the steam point is upper.
Do not use the Celsius-to-Fahrenheit formula when converting Fahrenheit to Celsius; use T_c = 5/9 (T_f − 32).
Do not forget the +273 when converting Celsius to Kelvin, or the temperature unit in the final answer.
Do not say that touch measures exact temperature; it only gives an idea of hotness or coldness.
Do not describe the liquid level as the temperature without explaining that the position of the end of the thread is read against the scale.
For thermometer-length problems, do not treat the length above the lower mark as the full fixed-point interval.
